## R24 — Form Post analytics (metadata only)

Two new contribution-event types, mirroring the poll events. **No table, no migration, no GraphQL schema change.**

| Event | Where | `id` | `name` | `space` | author |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CALLOUT_FORM_CREATED` | `createCalloutOnCalloutsSet`, **with** `CALLOUT_CREATED`, same gating as `CALLOUT_POLL_CREATED` (drafts included) | callout id | Form title, else the Post's `nameID` | level-zero space | creator |
| `FORM_RESPONSE_SUBMITTED` | `submitCalloutFormResponse`, **after** the response is committed, next to the notification dispatch | **response** id (one per response in MULTIPLE mode) | Form title, else `nameID` | level-zero space | submitter |

- 🔒 **No content in any document:** no answer text, selected options, prompts or option labels.
- **Never fails a mutation:** the reporter is fire-and-forget. A rejected submit (validation, closed form, SINGLE-mode duplicate, denied CONTRIBUTE) indexes nothing.
- **Level-zero space on submit:** read from the space the submit path already loads (`calloutsSet.collaboration.space.levelZeroSpaceID`), so no extra query. The Form row is loaded for its title.
- **No `updateCallout` hook**, unlike the switch-to-Form request in the issue comments. That path can't produce a Form Post: switching a framing to or from FORM is rejected with `FORM_FRAMING_FIXED_KIND` (`callout.framing.service.ts`). The hook would never fire.
- **Withdrawals** (own withdraw / admin delete) emit nothing, as the issue scopes them out.

## R25 — Polls and Forms in templates (server#6435)
- **Form permission on template paths only:** the Form framing permission (D-7) is passed only on the template paths:
  - callout-template creation;
  - template content-space creation (create/update a template from a space);
  - space and subspace creation from a template, whose creator becomes its admin;
  - `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate`.
- **Still refused:** the VC knowledge base, transfer and conversion. A Form in a create-space/subspace request's own callouts also stays refused (`FORM_FRAMING_NOT_ALLOWED`).
- **Space templates carry Polls and Forms, definitions only:**
  - Poll: title, options in order, settings. A new poll starts OPEN with 0 votes.
  - Form: title, description, questions **without ids**, settings as-is. Never responses.
- **Template Forms are definitions:**
  - `updateCalloutForm` on a standalone callout template requires UPDATE on the template callout.
  - `submitCalloutFormResponse` rejects any template with `FORM_TEMPLATE_NOT_RESPONDABLE`. A callout counts as a template when it **or its owning collaboration** is one. The flag is also now set on `updateTemplateFromSpace` / template-applier copies.
- **Template polls** no longer try to send notifications or contribution reports (that used to log errors).
- **VC knowledge bases** created from the platform knowledge template still receive no Poll or Form, the behaviour before R25.
- **Review:** a security review was run and its medium/low findings fixed with tests that failed before the fix. Older template capture/read permission gaps the review surfaced are recorded as separate follow-ups in the spec; they are not part of this PR.

## Tests
- `contribution.reporter.service.spec.ts`: both documents are indexed with the right type, id, name, space and author.
- `callouts.set.resolver.mutations.spec.ts`:
  - a Form Post reports both events, using the title or falling back to `nameID`, drafts included;
  - an ordinary posts callout reports no Form event.
- `callout.form.resolver.mutations.spec.ts`:
  - one event per stored response, with response id, title, level-zero space and submitter;
  - no answer content in the payload, and the `nameID` fallback;
  - nothing on a rejected submit or denied CONTRIBUTE.
- Gates: `biome check src/`, `tsc --noEmit`, full `vitest run` (11098 passed). Pre-commit green.

Fixes alkem-io/server#6329

Server half of the removal fix; the Matrix half is alkem-io/matrix-adapter#82. Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801 (Phase 1).

## Root cause

Removing a member from a group conversation deleted the Alkemio membership, but the Matrix kick was always rejected: every member holds the same power level, so nobody outranks anybody. The removed user stayed `join` in Synapse, kept receiving messages and could still post. Server side, three gaps made this worse:
- The "fall back to local removal only if the workflow threw" branch could never run: the event emitter logs a failing `room.member.updated` listener instead of rethrowing, so a failed workflow left the membership in place.
- A removal completed locally after a failed or timed-out RPC was later confirmed by Matrix's own leave, which published `MEMBER_REMOVED` a second time (and could delete the conversation twice).
- Room deletion removes the row before the Matrix room, so every member's later leave hit a room that no longer exists.

## Fix

- `completeLocalMemberRemoval` always ends with the idempotent row deletion.
- `handleConversationMemberLeft` acts only when its call actually removed the row (`persistMemberRemoved` now reports it), so a late leave is a no-op.
- `handleRoomMemberUpdated` ignores events for rooms that no longer exist (new `RoomLookupService.getRoom`).
- RPC transport failures (timeouts) take the local-removal path, as they already did; comments, the warning text and the docs now say so.
- `removeConversationMember` / `leaveConversation` GraphQL descriptions updated; `schema.graphql` regenerated (descriptions only).
- `docs/matrix-admin-reflection.md` Finding 1 rewritten for the new mechanism and its limits.

## Regression tests

- `message.inbox.service.spec.ts`: stale leave for a deleted room is ignored; a late leave after local removal publishes nothing.
- `conversation.service.spec.ts`, `conversation.resolver.mutations.spec.ts`: local removal always completes; rejected/timed-out removal paths.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run src/domain/communication/conversation` 76 passed; `message.inbox.service.spec` 25 passed.

## Verified end to end (local stack, this branch + alkem-io/matrix-adapter#82)

Before (develop): after removal B stayed `join` in Synapse, still received new messages and could send (event accepted); server log `Matrix kick rejected`.
After: B's own account leaves (`leave`, sender = B), new messages are not visible to B, B's send is rejected with `M_FORBIDDEN`, no "kick rejected" warning, `MEMBER_REMOVED` published once; voluntary leave and last-member auto-delete still work. Also run live: removal while the adapter was paused (the mutation waited out the RPC timeout, removed the row locally and published `MEMBER_REMOVED` once; the adapter's late leave was a no-op), and space-member removal (the Space's updates room was left through the member's own account; the Space's own bot kick never reaches Matrix because `communication.spaceID` is empty on that stack, which is the same on `develop` and untouched here).

## What went wrong

Every conversion and move mutation is gated on an in-memory policy built in the `ConversionResolverMutations` constructor. Its role list is the entire check — the policy is in-memory, so no credential rule in the database can widen it.

`67bc7945f` ("initial pass at updating global roles", May 2024) renamed the global role `global-admin-spaces` to `global-support`. Throughout that commit the symbol was renamed in place and kept in its lists:

```diff
-  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
+  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_SUPPORT,
```

At this one call site it was deleted instead of renamed:

```diff
-    [
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN,
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
-    ],
+    [AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN],
```

Holders of the role now called `global-support` silently lost access to all seven mutations sharing this policy: `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `convertSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertVirtualContributorToUseKnowledgeBase`.

It reads as a rename that missed a call site rather than a deliberate restriction — nothing in that commit suggests an intent to narrow conversions. **If the narrowing was intentional, this PR should be closed and #6536 answered instead**; I could not find anything recording that intent.

## What this changes

Restores `GLOBAL_SUPPORT` to the role list, and adds a test asserting the list. Nothing covered it before, which is exactly why the rename went unnoticed — the existing specs mock `grantAccessOrFail`, so they pass whatever the roles are.

This also realigns the gate with `createPlatformCredentialRules`, which grants `PLATFORM_ADMIN` to `global-admin`, `global-support` and `global-license-manager`. Before this change a caller could hold `PLATFORM_ADMIN` on the platform and still be refused here.

- `vitest run conversion.resolver.mutations.spec.ts` — 20 passed.

## Deliberately left out

Two things surfaced in #6536 that made this hard to diagnose but are separate changes:

- `global-license-manager` also holds `PLATFORM_ADMIN` platform-side but is not in this list. I have not added it — widening beyond restoring the lost role is a product call, not a regression fix.
- The failure logs `on authorization undefined of type 'in-memory'`, which reads like a missing policy and sends you looking in the database. The policy name is already passed to the constructor and would point straight at the real check.

QA re-tested #6021 after #6339 merged and acceptance criterion 3 ("same logic applies when the destination's innovation flow was changed via template", the alkem-io/client-web#9353 sequence) still failed: the transferred callout is tagged with one of the destination's **old** state names and shows on no flow tab.

## Root cause (proven at code level)

The transfer logic from #6339 is correct but validates against the destination's flow-state `TagsetTemplate` (`allowedValues` / `defaultSelectedValue`), and that template drifts from the `InnovationFlow`'s actual states through three writers:

1. **Template apply** — `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate` loads the target collaboration with `calloutsSet.tagsetTemplateSet` (eager `tagsetTemplates`, `cascade: true` on every hop). `updateInnovationFlowStates` updates a *separately loaded* copy of the template and saves it; the applier's final `collaborationService.save(targetCollaboration)` then cascades the **stale** in-memory template back over the row, reverting `allowedValues`/`defaultSelectedValue` to the pre-template names. Memo signing renders the live Yjs projection and resolves every internal image through document metadata and file-service bytes. ## What / why

A persona on the **generic** engine had no server-side route to receive a stored prompt graph: the invocation builder attached `promptGraph` only inside the `EXPERT` branch. So the declarative graph support merged in [virtual-contributor#122](https://github.com/alkem-io/virtual-contributor/pull/122) (conditional edges, retrieve/echo nodes, the shipped workshop payload) was live but **unreachable through configuration**.

This adds a `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES` allowlist covering `expert` + `generic-openai`, new GraphQL authoring fields for the node/edge forms, an activation guide, and the workshop authoring fixture.

Closes #6385. Spec: `workspace#053-generic-prompt-graph`.

## What actually changed in production code

Most of the diff is tests and docs, but **three source files change existing behaviour** — worth reading rather than skimming:

**`ai.persona.resolver.mutations.ts` — the `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` body was restructured, not extended.** The fetch and the authorization check moved inside a `try`, an audit call was added on both the success and failure paths, and a constructor dependency was added. **The authorization check is unchanged in substance and still runs before any update**: same `grantAccessOrFail`, same `AuthorizationPrivilege.UPDATE`, same policy object, same position relative to the mutation — only its enclosing block moved. That is the property to verify when reviewing this hunk, and it is why the restructure is called out here instead of being described as an addition.

**`ai.persona.service.ts` — two conditions changed.** `input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT` became `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES.includes(input.engine)`; that is the feature. A second condition was *tightened*: `if (!invocationGraph)` became `if (!invocationGraph && input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT)`, deliberately keeping the default-graph fallback expert-only so a generic persona with no stored graph produces **no `promptGraph` key at all** rather than inheriting expert's default.

**`prompt.graph.node.dto.ts` / `prompt.graph.edge.dto.ts` / `ai.persona.dto.update.ts`** add nullable fields; the only removal is an import line being widened.

Genuinely additive: every new test file, the docs, and the fixture. **No pre-existing test was modified or deleted** (`git diff origin/develop..HEAD -- '**/*.spec.ts' | grep -c '^-'` = 0), and the **GraphQL schema** delta is additive — 21 added, 0 breaking.

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **The story said "GENERIC"; there is no such enum value.** It is `AiPersonaEngine.GENERIC_OPENAI` (`generic-openai`) — the routing key bound to the `virtual-contributor-engine-generic` queue.
- **The allowlist deliberately excludes** `guidance`, `openai-assistant`, `libra-flow`, `community-manager`: widening requires engine-side graph execution first. A future enum value defaults to *not* attaching.
- **No validation of the graph/body-of-knowledge pairing.** `bodyOfKnowledgeID` is per-invocation from the VC, not stored on the persona, so the server cannot validate it. A retrieve-bearing graph on a BoK-less persona hard-fails at engine parse time and the member sees the standard error response — a documented precondition, not a defect.
- **No migration**: `ai_persona.promptGraph` jsonb already existed engine-independently.
- Expert behaviour is byte-identical in all three modes (stored / default / none).

## Evidence

- **Rebased 2026-10-06 onto `develop` `365de8f2b`** (was 140 commits behind). The three commits replay unchanged — the PR diff is identical to the reviewed head `e8321124` except `schema.graphql`, where develop had itself reworded an unrelated description. The old merge-from-develop commit (the only unsigned one) is gone; all three commits are signed.
- **`schema.graphql` regenerated** with `SCHEMA_BOOTSTRAP_LIGHT=1 pnpm run schema:print && pnpm run schema:sort` — output byte-identical to the rebased file. `schema:diff` against develop: **21 additive, 0 breaking**, 0 deprecated.
- Lint, typecheck, build clean. The PR's own specs: **52 / 52** across 4 files.
- Full suite **10 800 pass**. A different 3–4 tests timed out on each of two local runs under machine load average 61–184 (APM, forum sync, OIDC, auth-reset) — none touched by this PR, every one green in isolation, develop green under lighter load. **CI on this head: all 11 checks green, including the full `test` job** — the local timeouts were machine load, not the PR.
- `AiPersonaInvocationInput` remains **absent** from `schema.graphql` (count 0).
- The authoring fixture parses through the **actual merged VC engine parser** (`2920c83`): 8 nodes, 2 conditional edges, state model built. That parser is unchanged through VC **v0.4.0**, the release now going to acceptance.

## Review round (8 findings, all fixed, 0 declined)

Two independent reviewers on different providers found non-overlapping defects:

**Security** (verdict was `conditional`, now remediated):
- `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` wrote **no audit record** — a global admin could change the graph governing prompts, retrieval and member output with no attributable trace. Now audits success *and* failure with actor / persona / engine / `promptGraphChanged` only; never the graph, prompt text or credentials (SOC 2 CC7.2·CC7.3, ISO A.8.15·A.8.16). **This is what motivated the resolver restructure described above.**
- The activation guide didn't disclose that retrieve nodes send body-of-knowledge content to the **external model provider**; it now requires a data-classification check before activation.
- `edge.map` was an unbounded JSON scalar → now bounded (string→string, 100 entries, 128 chars per key/value). Structural limits only; graph semantics stay the engine's job.

**Correctness** — two of these were caught by *mutating the production code and watching the tests stay green*:
- The **round-trip test was tautological**: the mocked repository assigns by reference, so it compared an object to itself. Gutting the transformer left it passing. It now crosses the transformer/JSON seam against a separately constructed object.

- **`schema.graphql` had been hand-authored**, including a *fabricated* description for the JSON scalar and wrong field ordering (~80 lines of divergence from the generator). ## What

The **Add to Post** and **Responses** strips in the create/edit callout dialog rendered every option as a flat row of neutral chips, with a flat primary navy for whatever was selected. Two changes, one commit each:

**1 · Three surfaced, the rest behind More**

| | Row | Behind More |
|---|---|---|
| **Add to Post** | Whiteboard · Memo · Media Gallery | Document, Call to Action, Poll, Contributors, Subspaces |
| **Responses** | Links & Files · Posts · Tasks | Memos, Whiteboards, Documents |

**2 · A hue per kind of content**

Whiteboard blue · Memo purple · Document teal · Call to Action orange · Media Gallery rose · Poll amber · Contributors emerald · Subspaces indigo. Responses reuses the shared three and adds Links & Files emerald, Posts amber, Tasks indigo.

## Why

Every new framing type and response type made the row longer and the dialog taller, pushing the title and description — the thing people opened the dialog to write — further out of view. A flat row also gives the least-used option exactly as much of the opening screen as the most-used one.

The surfaced three come from Sept 2026 usage: whiteboard 162, memo 97, media gallery 73; links & files 324.

**Caveat, from the analyst, worth keeping in mind for review:** the counts measure *activity on* a type rather than *creation of* one, and cannot separate "added to a post" from "asked for as a response". That is good enough to pick three; it is not good enough to order the menu, which keeps `CHIPS` order.

On colour: nothing about a chip said which kind of content it was except its label, and every selection looked identical. The hue is on the icon in every state — a colour you first see after picking is one nobody learns — and selection fills the chip with that kind's own colour instead of navy.

## The two colour rules, both tested

`chipTints.ts` holds the mapping in one place so the strips cannot drift apart. `chipTints.test.ts` asserts both rules:

1. **A concept keeps its hue across both strips.** A whiteboard is blue whether you attach one or ask people to contribute one back. `whiteboard`, `memo` and `document` appear in both and share a key.
2. **Hues are unique within a strip.** Two chips visible at once never share a colour. Across strips they may — Poll (framing) and Posts (responses) are both amber — because the strips sit in separate sections and each holds one selection.

Values are the Tailwind 100/600 pairs the design system already uses for tinted icons, so this reuses a vocabulary the product has rather than adding one. Colour is never the only signal: selection is still carried by the fill, the `×` affordance and `aria-checked`.

## Behaviour that is deliberately preserved

- **The More trigger sits beside the radiogroup, not inside it.** It is a way to reach the other options, not an option — announcing it as the fourth radio would be wrong.
- **A type chosen from the menu joins the row** and takes the selection, so a less common choice is never hidden once it has been made, and stays clearable without reopening the menu.
- **Edit mode / `locked`:** the trigger is disabled and greyed with the same lock hint the frozen chips carry, so the row does not change shape between create and edit.
- **`disabledChips`:** entitlement-gated types grey out in the menu and keep their tooltip. They are inert via `aria-disabled` plus a prevented `onSelect` rather than Radix's `disabled`, which sets `pointer-events: none` and would swallow the reason.
- **`allowedChips`:** under five available types everything renders flat, so consumers that narrow the list (templates, a VC knowledge base) are unaffected.
- **Tasks** keeps the third Responses slot when the consumer offers it. When it does not — edit mode, flag off, or posts disallowed — Whiteboards takes that slot so the row still reads as three.

## Scope

`CalloutFormConnector` is **not** touched. The components' props are unchanged, and nothing about what renders *after* a selection changes — that is the connector's framing and response zones.

## Testing

- `forms/callout/`: 91 tests pass (12 rewritten to go through the menu, 11 added for the menu behaviour, 7 added for the colour rules)

- i18n parity across all six languages passes; `More` + menu heading added to `en, nl, es, bg, de, fr`

## Still open for the reviewer

**Document is now behind More.** Correct on the numbers (20 uses) but it shipped recently — if anyone is pushing its adoption, they may want to weigh in before this merges.

Conversation messaging moves to the browser's own Matrix session: sign-in, reads and writes for conversation rooms go straight to Synapse. Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801. Stories: alkem-io/client-web#10157 (session), alkem-io/client-web#10158 (reads), alkem-io/client-web#10159 (writes). Specs: alkem-io/agents-hq#122, alkem-io/agents-hq#163, alkem-io/agents-hq#164.

Replaces alkem-io/client-web#10215: this branch contains all of its commits plus the read and write work.

## What changes

**Session**
- Silent SSO in a hidden iframe → one-time `loginToken` → `POST /_matrix/client/v3/login`. Per-user IndexedDB credential record; every Matrix namespace cleared on Alkemio sign-out; no server-side Matrix logout.
- `/matrix-callback` page (nginx location + Vite entry); the SSO `redirectUrl` is always the platform origin, so innovation-hub subdomains work.
- A rejected token gets one silent re-login and one restart, then fails closed (no retry loop).

**Reads** (conversation rooms only)
- `<MatrixSession/>` mounted at the root; sync starts for every signed-in user.
- Latest message, live timeline, reactions, deletions: from `/sync`. Opening a conversation backfills up to ~1,000 events.
- Unread count: same rule matrix-adapter used (walk back to `m.fully_read`, ~285 events, fall back to Synapse's count).
- Read receipts: one `/read_markers` call setting `m.fully_read` and `m.read`, only while the tab is visible and focused.
- Attachments on media events resolved through the new `Room.messageAttachments` field (alkem-io/server#6574).
- The conversation list, membership and lifecycle stay on GraphQL; a room not in `me.conversations` is never shown.
- Chat sound and badge triggered by sync with the same rules.

**Writes**
- Text, react and unreact sent straight to Synapse. A send resolves only once Synapse accepts the event; a failed send removes its local echo and keeps the draft with the existing "send not confirmed" error.
- DM text sends check the counterpart's `isContactable` before every send (`ActorDetails`, network-only), as `sendMessageToRoom` did; a failed lookup blocks the send. Attachment sends still go through `sendMessageToRoom`, which keeps the server-side check.
- Attachments, comments, forum, updates and calendar rooms are unchanged (GraphQL).

**Known differences**
- A failed direct send shows only the "send not confirmed" error and keeps the draft; the global Apollo error toast no longer appears for it. A failed react or unreact shows the generic error toast.
- The composer clears its text when Send is pressed and restores it if the send is not confirmed.
- A message in the first seconds after page load does not sound (a room is watched only after the badge's ~2 s ready-delay), and neither does the first message of a conversation created after page load. The sound also plays for live edits, URL-less stickers and bodyless non-media messages from non-web Matrix clients, which the adapter skipped.

## Depends on
- Server: `Room.messageAttachments` (alkem-io/server#6574), deployed first: the query requests `pending`.
- Environment: Synapse `sso.client_whitelist` and `VITE_APP_MATRIX_HOMESERVER_URL` (alkem-io/dev-orchestration#97). Acceptance/production config is not part of this PR.

## Checks
- `tsc`, biome, full vitest suite: 482 files / 4217 tests pass (the `budgetMeter` test needs an en_US locale, unrelated).
- Local end-to-end run on an isolated stack: session, reads and writes scenarios pass; not run live: innovation-hub subdomain SSO, a missing-actor SSO claim.

Fixes alkem-io/server#6329

## Root cause

The bot creates every Alkemio room (power level 100) but leaves it once members join, so users never see it. Every member holds power level 50. Synapse lets a sender kick only a target it **strictly** outranks, so in a room nobody can kick anybody. Removing a member (`HandleBatchRemoveMember` → `KickUser`) therefore always failed with `M_FORBIDDEN`: `getIntentForRoom` picked a same-rank member as the kicker.

This PR addresses only cause 1 from the issue (the Matrix-side rejection). Cause 2 (authorization policy never reset on reapply) is already fixed on `server` `develop`.

## Fix

`KickUser` (`internal/infrastructure/matrix/mautrix.go`) is now the room path only. It removes a user as follows:

- **Target joined, invited or knocking:** the target's own ghost leaves the room (`EnsureRegistered` first). The operator's reason is not attached, since Matrix would record it as the member's own statement.
- **Target with no membership** (never joined, e.g. a forum discussion or community updates room, or already left): nothing is sent, and the removal is reported as forbidden (`NOT_ALLOWED`), the same result the old kick returned. No leave event would follow, so reporting success would leave the server waiting for one and the member could never be removed there.

A failure to read the room's memberships is returned as an error, not treated as success. The bot is never brought back into a room, so the timeline never shows "bot joined / bot left".

**Spaces are unchanged from `develop`.** `KickFromSpace` kicks with the bot, which stays a member of spaces and outranks every user. Space callers (`space_service.go`) already know they hold a space, so no room type is read.

Callers of the room path: batch member removal (group conversations, forum discussions, community updates rooms) in `handler_room.go`, and room deletion (`DeleteRoomFully`) in `room_service.go`. `MatrixPort` is unchanged; the `KickUser` contract is documented on the port.

## Commit history

The branch has six commits, kept as-is:
1. `baf2c6d` made the removed member leave for every batch removal. That returned 403 "not in room" for users who never joined a room.
2. `3d84c6c` kicked with an account that outranks the target, admin-joining the bot when needed. That made the bot visible in the room timeline.
3. `fce20f7` removed room members by their own leave and dropped the bot re-admission, keeping the membership check from (2).
4. `1fdc532` reports a target with no membership as a failed removal instead of a silent success.
5. `102aaba` stopped `KickFromSpace` from going through `KickUser`, which at that point read the room type first.
6. `d950e47` removed the space branch from `KickUser`; it is the room path only, and `KickFromSpace` kicks directly as before.

## Behaviour notes

- **Matrix history.** A removed room member shows as "X left", never "X was removed". A voluntary leave (`leaveConversation` goes through the same removal) now reads accurately.
- **Listener.** `listener.go` `handleMembershipEvent` emits the same `leave` event whether the member left or was kicked; the server's `handleRoomMemberUpdated` does not look at who acted.
- **Companion server change:** alkem-io/server#6573.
  - the group-conversation local-removal fallback always completes;
  - a late leave after a timed-out removal is a no-op;
  - leave events for rooms already deleted are ignored, since room deletion now makes every member really leave.

## Tests

- In `mautrix_intent_test.go`, `TestKickUser_Room_TargetLeaves` (join, invite, knock), `TestKickUser_Room_NotInRoomIsForbidden`, `TestKickUser_Room_LeaveError` and `TestKickUser_MembershipReadErrorPropagates` replace the old space-kick `KickUser` tests. They assert the target's own intent leaves and no other intent acts or joins, and that `domain.ErrForbidden` is returned for never-joined and already-left targets.
- `TestHandleBatchRemoveMember_RemovalRejected` (`handler_room_test.go`): a rejected removal is returned as a per-room `ErrCodeNotAllowed`, never as a success.
- `TestKickFromSpace_*` keep covering the space kick.
- `go test ./...`, `make build` and `make lint` (0 issues) pass.
- Verified end to end together with alkem-io/server#6573 on a local stack: the removed member's own account leaves, new messages are not visible to them, and their send is rejected with `M_FORBIDDEN`.

## Code comments

This PR touches code comments; none reference specs, issues, or PR numbers.

  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>

- Evacuate endpoints ([#​8443](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8443))
  - The new `$JS.API.SERVER.EVACUATE` endpoint can safely evacuate streams, and any consumers on those streams, from a node
  - The new `$JS.API.STREAM.PEER.EVACUATE.*` endpoint can safely evacuate a peer, and any consumers on that peer, from a stream
  - These operations combined allow for maintenance operations with full transfer of data and state without having to peer-remove first
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>

Two client-driven E2E realignments found while triaging the 2026-08-31 nightly reds, plus a stabilization of the callout full-workflow spec.

### 1. Contributors-callout suite → client feature 025 (FR-012)

Client feature 025 (callout manual selection, client-web#10048) changed the rendering contract: the segmented type switch derives from the **resolved** collection — segments render only for types with a non-zero count, and the switch is hidden below two resolved types (supersedes 008 FR-009a's configured-types gate).

- **1.3** asserts the resolved-types switch: People + Organizations segments with counts, **no** segment for the configured-but-empty Virtual Contributors type.
- **1.4** rewritten: a multi-type callout resolving to a single non-zero type renders no switch at all (the pre-025 "VC segment empty state" scenario is unreachable without a community VC).
- **1.7** excludes Organizations (a resolved type) so edit persistence stays observable.
- **1.5–1.8** made partial-run-proof (`ensureMainCallout()` + `waitForContentFeed()`) so `--last-failed` / `-g` subsets can't strand tests that depended on 1.3 having run.
- `specs/009` spec.md: revision note, amended US2/US3, and a **VC-seeding feasibility note** (`assignRoleToVirtualContributor` probed working end-to-end on local; lib helper is a follow-up).

### 2. Whiteboard E2E → local-first editor (close-to-save)

The whiteboard editor rework (client-web#10205/#10207/#10241 era) changed the contract: the editor dialog is named after the whiteboard (the `Drawing canvas` filter text no longer exists), the **Save button is gone** (autosave + durable close via *Close whiteboard*), *Find Template* moved to the editor header, and materializing a template's drawing renames the outer dialog Create→"Edit whiteboard template".

- `whiteboard-dialog.ts`: dialog located via the stable *Close whiteboard* button; new `closeWhiteboardEditor()` replaces every editor Save click (3 consumers migrated).
- `whiteboard-template.spec.ts` 1.1/1.3 retargeted to the renamed dialog; `instructions.md` selector map updated.

### 3. Callout full-workflow spec → worker- and retry-safe

`0.1callout-full-workflow.spec.ts` chained five steps across three fixture describes on module-level `Date.now()` callout names. That only holds when every describe runs in the same worker: local `fullyParallel` can split them, a retry always gets a fresh worker (fresh module eval => fresh name), and running a single step in isolation never runs the sibling that created the entity.

- The admin-created callout name is assigned in the Step 1/2 `beforeAll` (one serial worker) instead of at module level.
- The outer `beforeAll` seeds a **published** callout via `createCalloutOnCalloutsSet`; Steps 3–5 open that instead of the Step-1 UI callout, so any subset of tests works in any worker.
- The moderation `beforeAll` seeds a post contribution and a comment through the API so Step 5's `> 0` assertions hold when it runs alone.
- Fixed 1s+3s post-render delay replaced by a 15s poll; per-step timeouts raised to 60s to clear `clickCallout`'s 30s hydration wait (previously surfaced as "Target page closed").
- `CollaborationPage.openCallout()` now retries the `Open {title}` click up to three times with a reload in between — a freshly created DRAFT callout can be missing from the feed rendered at navigation time, so waiting on that page alone never surfaces it.

Durable Playwright cover for **workspace#051-cleverbase-account-linking** — the Connected Accounts section on Security settings, shipped in alkem-io/client-web#10176 (merged to `develop` 2026-08-24).

The forge run's Phase-V acceptance walks were driven ad-hoc and **persisted no specs** — its own ledger recorded *"Emitted @forge-acceptance specs: none persisted … the durable-spec follow-up can ride the test-suites flow."* This is that follow-up.

## Coverage — 13 cases, 7 files

`client-web/src/functional-e2e/connected-accounts/`

| Case | What it pins |
|---|---|
| CA-01 | three provider rows *Not connected* + Connect, read-only credential rows, no identity leakage |
| CA-02 | credential rows route via in-page anchors to the password/passkey cards, no inline mutation |
| CA-05 | a password error stays inside the password card (does not echo into the section) |
| CA-06 | owner-only: a platform admin on another user's security URL is redirected, no settings flow created |
| CA-04 | fail-closed when the settings flow is unreadable — explicit error + retry, **zero** provider rows; retry recovers in place |
| CA-03 / CA-07 | last-method lock shows a focusable `aria-disabled` Disconnect carrying its reason; curing the lock flips the same row to enabled |
| CA-30 / CA-31 | disconnect requires the confirm dialog — confirming POSTs `unlink=<provider>` with zero provider contact, Cancel fires no POST |
| CA-20 / CA-21 | Connect natively POSTs `link=<provider>` + CSRF to the flow action and writes the outcome marker; returning from an interrupted Connect announces the retry notice once |
| CA-40 / CA-42 / CA-43 / CA-43b | errored-flow resume (`4000007`) on bare `/settings`, and each outcome announcement — pending, connected, disconnected — exactly once |
| CA-41 | regression: the recovery-born settings flow still renders *Set new password* on bare `/settings` (the T027 resume seam) |

Live dev stack throughout; Kratos settings-flow **reads** are mocked only where a state cannot be provoked deterministically (locked rows, unreadable flow, completed round-trips). All URLs resolve at runtime from each persona's own profile URL — never a hardcoded `/user/<slug>`.

## Harness changes these depend on

- **`authenticated-session.fixture.ts`** — persona sessions are validated against Kratos `whoami` before reuse, and gain `maxSessionAgeSeconds`. Kratos gates privileged self-service operations behind `privileged_session_max_age` (15m); a live-but-stale cached session makes a privileged submit redirect to a re-auth screen instead of returning the expected settings-flow response. Specs doing privileged work now re-mint rather than mis-assert.
- **`config/global-setup.ts`** — provision personas through the Kratos **admin** API when `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` is reachable (deterministic; no HIBP/self-service policy; a reset Kratos store heals on the next run instead of timing out every login), falling back to self-service registration otherwise. Then warm every persona's storage state **serially, before any worker exists** — concurrent cold logins were blowing the 30s budget as `Test timeout … exceeded while setting up storageState`. Warm-up failures are deliberately non-fatal so only the affected specs go red, attributably.
- **`getRecoveryLink(recipientEmail?)`** — the MailSlurper inbox is shared. An unfiltered subject match could open **another suite's** recovery mail and complete recovery against it, silently resetting that persona's harness credential for the rest of the run. `authentication-password-recovery.spec.ts` updated to pass its own address.

## Gates

- `tsc --noEmit` clean — `client-web` and `lib`
- `eslint` clean on every new/changed file
- Commit GPG-signed

## Run results — 15 / 16 green

Run against the local dev stack (client-web on `develop` incl. the merged #10176; Traefik origin `:3000`), `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` set so `global-setup` provisions personas through the Kratos admin API.

| Run | Workers | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (3.1m) |
| 2 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (1.9m) |
| 3 | 1 | 15 passed, 1 failed (2.2m) |

The 15 are stable and fast (1.5-4.7s each) across all three runs — every case that exercises Connected Accounts itself is green.

### The one failure is NOT a test defect and NOT 051

**CA-41** times out at its first UI step, waiting for `Forgot password?`, with the login page frozen on *"Preparing secure sign-in…"*. Root cause reproduced with **zero test code involved** — a bare fresh browser context hitting `/login` directly:

```
401 /api/auth/oidc/id-token-hint | 302 /api/auth/oidc/login | 302 /oidc/login
303 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser
200 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser     <-- flow created TWICE
403 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/flows?id=...
{"error":{"id":"security_csrf_violation","code":403, ...}}
```

Two defects, both on the **login/OIDC bootstrap** — a surface 051 does not touch:

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  ## Raised separately

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.
